USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold the existing Section 301 package in place and use the already-scheduled January 1, 2019 List 3 step-up from 10% to 25% as bargaining leverage, but do not add a new tariff tranche or non-tariff blow before the planned Trump–Xi meeting at the G-20. Reopen senior talks aimed at structural IP, forced tech-transfer, and industrial-subsidy commitments—not another May-style purchase pledge. Pair talks with continued farm-channel relief and bilateral deals that raise China’s cost of waiting, without conceding rollbacks that have not been earned.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is real but not high. The March 22 Section 301 finding documented IP/tech-transfer practices that cut against US technology leadership, and by September 24 the US had tariffs on ~$250B of Chinese goods while China had answered with matching $50B plus 5–10% on ~$60B, concentrated on soy, autos, and other politically exposed exports. That retaliation is biting: US goods exports to China fell from $10.4B in May to $9.2B in October (−11.6%), soybean prices dropped ~20%, and USDA had to authorize up to $12B in Market Facilitation and related aid (about $3.6B of the first $4.7B aimed at soy). The goods deficit also widened (BOPGTB −$66.6B to −$76.5B) as imports from China were front-run (IMPCH +18.7%). CNY depreciation of ~9.7% (6.32 to 6.93) blunts part of the tariff wedge. Those are genuine costs, so the score is not an opportunity reading.

They are not a +0.5 reading either. US activity is still firm (UMCSENT 98.6, INDPRO up ~1.5% in the window, CPI contained), the Fed is hiking from a position of strength (FF 2.19%), and China is absorbing more financial stress (Shanghai cited ~−25% YTD in the Oct 4 Pence speech; Chinese reserves down ~$56B). List 3 only took effect September 24; the unused remainder of the import base and the locked Jan 1 25% hike remain unused leverage. Escalating now—especially into consumer goods, or via another ZTE-style shock—would raise US prices, invite further farm/auto retaliation, and collide with the mid-October vol spike (VIX 11.6 on Oct 3 to 25.0 on Oct 11) plus midterms. The May 19 joint statement showed that a purchase-only truce does not survive; the White House correctly restarted 301 ten days later. The right stance is therefore negotiate at 0: test whether Beijing will put structural remedies on the table at the G-20 channel reported October 11, keep current tariffs and the scheduled rate hike as the walk-away, and do not unilaterally escalate or roll back.
key_factors: Section 301 IP/tech-transfer case remains the core US interest and is still unremedied
US has ~$250B already tariffed and a locked Jan 1 List 3 hike to 25% as unused leverage
China retaliation is hitting US farm exports (soy ~-20%, EXPCH -11.6%) and required a $12B USDA bridge
US real economy still strong; China showing more FX/reserve/equity stress, but CNY -9.7% offsets some tariff bite
G-20 Trump-Xi meeting is teed up; midterms and the mid-October VIX spike argue against a new escalation tranche
May purchase-only truce collapsed in 10 days — talks must demand structural commitments, not concede rollbacks

sources_cited.excerpt: USTR Section 301 report finds China's IP/tech-transfer practices unreasonable; Trump directs tariffs, WTO case, and investment restrictions.
Joint statement: China to 'significantly increase' purchases; Mnuchin says trade war 'on hold.' Truce later collapsed.
White House announces US will proceed with Section 301 25% tariffs on ~$50B; truce collapses.
Trump directs USTR to finalize List 3: 10% on ~$200B effective Sept 24, scheduled to rise to 25% on Jan 1, 2019.
List 3 takes effect at 10%. China retaliates 5–10% on ~$60B. Combined US 301 coverage ~$250B.
US exports to China fell from $10.40B (May) to $9.19B (Oct), -11.6% over the window.
US imports from China rose from $43.87B (May) to $52.08B (Oct), +18.7%, consistent with tariff front-running.
US goods trade deficit widened from -$66.6B (May) to -$76.5B (Oct).
CNY weakened from 6.32 to 6.93 per USD (+9.7%), offsetting part of the US tariff.
VIX jumped from 11.61 (Oct 3) to 24.98 (Oct 11), still 17.4 on Oct 17 — market stress after List 3.
Michigan sentiment still high at 98.6 in October; US domestic demand not breaking.
USDA up to $12B farm aid; initial MFP ~$4.7B, of which ~$3.63B for soybeans at $1.65/bu.
China bought nearly a third of US soybeans in 2017; soybean prices down about $2/bu or 20% since June.
Trump and Xi agreed to meet at the G-20 in Buenos Aires, first direct talks since August.
Pence (Oct 4): $250B in tariffs targeting advanced industries China wants; threat to more than double unless a fair deal; Shanghai -25% YTD cited as impact.
After USMCA/Korea, US pursuing bilateral Asian deals to pressure China ahead of a possible November Trump-Xi meeting.
